accessibility.contrast_body_a: Text and interface colors are token-pairs checked against the AA ratios (4.5:1 text, 3:1 components); the quiet text tiers step up automatically under
accessibility.contrast_body_b: . Color never carries meaning alone — every status pairs a label or icon with its hue, and the map layers use the Wong colorblind-safe palette.
accessibility.feedback_before: If anything here is hard to perceive, operate, or understand, that is a defect in the design contract — report it to the
accessibility.feedback_cite: Voting and candidacy require nothing beyond living in the place you are voting in — the interface must not add barriers the constitution forbids · Art. I
accessibility.feedback_mid: so it is fixed before the production build inherits it. You can also
accessibility.focus_body: A 3-pixel gold ring marks focus on every control; under Windows contrast themes the same outline renders in the system highlight color. Sticky chrome reserves scroll padding so the focused element is never hidden behind it.
accessibility.i18n_body: All layout uses CSS logical properties so right-to-left scripts mirror correctly (flip the direction from the Demo controls to verify); the language switcher sits in the header on every page; a pseudo-locale with 35% text expansion is part of the QA toolchain.
accessibility.intro: Representation for every one of us means an interface every one of us can operate — across ability, language, script direction, device, and connection. This statement covers the mockup site itself and records the accessibility contract the production build inherits.
accessibility.keyboard_body: Every interaction works without a pointer: a skip link is the first focusable element on every page, header menus are native disclosure widgets (Escape closes them), the ranked ballot uses move buttons rather than drag-only ordering, and flow walkthroughs are plain buttons and links.
accessibility.limit_copy: Page body copy ships in English; the locale switcher translates the application chrome only. The production build externalizes every string through an ICU MessageFormat catalog per the internationalization plan.
accessibility.limit_demo: The Demo controls at the foot of each screen are a demonstration instrument, not part of the application contract.
accessibility.limit_map: The stylized map panes (jurisdiction browser, district mapper) are placement stand-ins for the developed Leaflet viewers; each carries a text description, and the adjacent panel presents the same data as text. The production viewers ship with full keyboard navigation and text equivalents.
accessibility.limit_testing: Automated and structural checks run on every page of this site; assistive-technology walkthroughs with human testers (screen reader, switch, voice control) are scheduled against the production build, not these static mockups.
accessibility.motion_body_a: Animations are sub-300ms, nothing flashes, and
accessibility.offline_body: Fonts are self-hosted (SIL OFL 1.1) and no resource loads from any external service — the site runs fully on a LAN with no internet access, on low-power hardware.
accessibility.reflow_body: Layouts hold from 320 CSS pixels (and at 400% zoom) through phone, tablet, and large monitors, portrait or landscape, with no horizontal scrolling and no orientation lock.
accessibility.review_line: Target: WCAG 2.2 Level AA, with some Level AAA · EN 301 549 · last reviewed 2026-06-11
accessibility.structure_body: Every page declares its language, carries a unique title, one h1, ordered heading levels, and the full landmark set (banner, navigation, main, contentinfo); status updates are announced through a persistent polite live region.
accessibility.timeouts_body: Constitutional clocks on these screens are simulated displays — nothing on the mockup site expires or auto-advances.
accessibility.touch_body: Interactive elements are at least 24×24 CSS pixels including the compact chip controls.
amendments.about: This screen shows the two ways the constitution can change — the settings door runs through the amendable setting change and the ordinary bill flow, and every change is sealed in the audit chain. Amendable settings are scoped per jurisdiction; ratification climbs the nesting chain through constituent supermajorities. In engineering terms, the hardened layer is a set of protected files guarded by the constitutional test suite — a release deploys only when the full suite passes.
amendments.check_not_allowed: “{value}” is not in the allowed set ({set}).
amendments.check_not_number: “{value}” is not a number — this setting takes {range}.
amendments.check_out_range: {value} is out of range — the engine would refuse it pre-vote (allowed {min} – {max}).
amendments.current_body_a: What every amendable setting is set to right now at the instance root, with the hardened range it must stay inside, and the act that last changed it. Values are scoped per jurisdiction — this is the instance-wide snapshot; the full inheritance-aware register is on the
amendments.door_one_body: Settings the constitution leaves to each jurisdiction, changed by a valid legislative act (an amendable setting change) through the ordinary bill flow. The engine blocks out-of-range values before the vote is even scheduled. Every applied change lands here, on the live ledger — appended, never edited.
amendments.door_two_body_a: Mechanics no act, admin panel, or office can touch. A change here is a new release of the software that must pass every automated constitutional check before it ships —
amendments.door_two_body_b: , in the open, with the change and its checks on the public record.
amendments.door_two_body_strong: softening exists only through this door
amendments.floor_body_a: The supermajority fraction is amendable, but its definition has a hardened floor: no redefinition may produce a threshold below
amendments.floor_body_b: of all serving members. The default is two thirds, computed as
amendments.floor_gloss: Supermajority, glossed: the share of every seated member — vacant seats still count in the denominator until refilled — so absence can never lower the bar.
amendments.intro: The constitution changes through exactly two doors. The settings it leaves open move by ordinary legislative acts, inside locked bounds. The locked core itself (the hardened layer) moves only by a new release of the software, made in the open with every constitutional check passing publicly. Nothing changes silently, and nothing changes any other way.
amendments.no_amendments: No amendments yet — every change will appear here, appended, never edited.

amendments.ratify_caption: Ratification thresholds by kind of change

amendments.ratify_within_threshold: Valid legislative act (majority or supermajority per the setting)
amendments.releases_sealed: Releases are sealed in the audit chain
amendments.rule_cgc_ip: Common-good-corporation intellectual property perpetually public domain
amendments.rule_districts: Districts of 5–9 seats — a chamber above 9 subdivides into districts; the chamber total itself has no ceiling
amendments.rule_quorum: Quorum & supermajority counted against all serving members
amendments.rule_residency: Voting & candidacy: residency only, no other requirements
amendments.rule_voting: Proportional voting with the Droop quota — never first-past-the-post or plurality
amendments.try_body: A pre-vote hint only. The engine runs the same bounds check server-side when the amendment bill is filed — this screen enacts nothing.

atlas.econ_lead: Money is an abstract unit of account — no payment rails, no custody. A wallet is private, like a ballot.
atlas.growth_note: Growth and reach are shown to celebrate participation and keep the network honest — never as a lever on anyone’s rights.
atlas.intro: One screen for the whole game: a living map of every node, place, organization, and willing resident — and the vital signs of representation, justice, the economy, and the mesh. The health of the world, and of everyone playing it.
atlas.land_note: Land is a simplified outline drawn for orientation. Positions are city-level and approximate.
atlas.living_map_gloss: Every node, place, organization, and opt-in resident on one Earth. Approximate positions only — this is orientation, not surveillance.
atlas.mesh_lead: Volunteer-run — keeping the world online buys no vote and no seat. If one node survives, the world survives.
atlas.no_rollup_body: The nightly world snapshot has not run on this instance, so the vital signs read as gaps rather than zeros.
atlas.optin_said: You now appear as a single approximate pixel — grid-snapped, no name attached.
atlas.people_lead: Individual achievements are private by default and confer no governance advantage — hard-separated from votes, seats, and money.
atlas.reach_gloss_a: Reach is the share of a place that is verified and present. It is a
atlas.reach_gloss_strong: display-only transparency gauge — never a governance input
atlas.reach_no_nights: Not enough measured nights yet to draw a trend. A withheld night is a gap, never a zero.

atlas.simulated_body: These are the vital signs of a demonstration instance, not a live civilization.
audit_chain.about_p1: Each entry's hash covers the previous entry's hash plus its own payload, making changes detectable. Rejected filings are recorded too, with the reason for refusal. Existing entries cannot be edited or deleted.
audit_chain.about_p2: This viewer shows published metadata. It does not expose the underlying payload or participant identities. Sequence numbers can have gaps, so the latest sequence number is not a count of entries.
audit_chain.about_p3a: The chain begins with the genesis previous hash
audit_chain.about_p3c: Full verification recalculates the links; browsing a receipt does not verify it.

clocks.about: The scheduler itself is the engine behind term synchronization and 90-day meeting enforcement. This page doubles as the scheduler spec — the production scheduler implements exactly these clock records, one row, one trigger source. Amendable defaults change by legislative act; hardened and structural clocks are fixed in code. Clocks themselves hold no state — they move other things (elections, emergency powers, vacancies, residency claims) through their stages.
clocks.default_derived: derived — see the workflow it fires
clocks.family_deadlines_desc: Countdowns, rolling deadlines, and bounded or continuous windows.
clocks.family_intervals_desc: Recurring and derived schedules — the clocks that re-arm themselves.
clocks.family_thresholds_desc: Quantity watchers — population, headcount, signatures, seats.
clocks.glossary: Glossary: quorum here always counts all serving members, never just those present; the Droop quota is the smallest vote count that mathematically guarantees a seat; the number of ballot finalists grows with the seats in the race.
clocks.intro: The scheduled sweeps that drive the world — every interval, deadline, window, and threshold that starts a process without anyone asking. Time and population do the triggering; officials never do, and nothing here needs a human to remember it.
clocks.playtest_body: Pulls every registered deadline closer instead of touching the wall clock — audit-marked as a dev action, dry run rendered before anything moves.
clocks.reading_amendable_body: means a valid legislative act can change the default within fixed bounds — see

clocks.reading_fire_body: Every fire event is appended to the
clocks.reading_live_body: is what the scheduler is actually holding right now — armed timers and the soonest real deadline, straight from the timer table.
clocks.reading_type_body: is the scheduler contract: recurring intervals re-arm on fire; countdowns expire once; windows open and close; thresholds watch a quantity and fire on crossing.
constitutional_questions.about_a: A margin note beside the amendment surface, not a second amendment door. Amendments to the running system go through the two doors on
constitutional_questions.about_b: ; this ledger records questions the constitutional text under-determined and the answers the build settled on (WF-SYS-05).
constitutional_questions.how_lands_a: A question qualifies when the constitutional text under-determines a mechanism the software must decide — and the build picks an answer. The entry names only the part of the text touched, states the implemented answer in one paragraph, and describes the surfaces where the answer is visible. Every
constitutional_questions.how_lands_b: marker elsewhere in the app resolves to its anchor here
constitutional_questions.intro_a: Places where building the game forced a decision the constitution's text didn't make. This is the home of the open "why" debates — each entry records the question, the answer the build chose, and where to see it working. Every
constitutional_questions.intro_b: marker across the app links here, and the whole list seeds the next draft of
constitutional_questions.ledger_body: Entries are appended as the build surfaces new questions; existing entries are only ever extended, never rewritten. Each entry records the constitutional text touched, what the attempt to build it surfaced, the implemented answer, and a status badge tracking it toward the post-game redraft.
constitutional_questions.q1_answer_c: can endorse any candidate; members with no endorsing organization stand on equal footing.
constitutional_questions.q1_surfaced: the running experiment removed the faction layer entirely. STV satisfies factional-makeup matching at the individual-preference level with no party layer; observer/audit standing transfers to endorsing organizations and candidates.
constitutional_questions.q1_touches: Touches: proportional voting systems · election security and integrity · committees · composition and selection of executive committees
constitutional_questions.q1_where: the open ballot filters by endorsing organization or individual endorsements with no party column anywhere; the committee surfaces show proportionality staying legible through endorsements alone. Observer and audit standing during counts transfers to endorsing organizations and the candidates themselves.
constitutional_questions.q2_answer: ties go to the seat holder with the largest share of votes after normalizing quotas — preserving the proportionality the STV election produced and one-person-one-vote, with no faction layer.
constitutional_questions.q2_surfaced: the constitutional tie-break ("each member's own 1st-choice vote performance in the prior election") assumes raw 1st-choice counts are comparable — but STV quota transfers make them incommensurable across winners.
constitutional_questions.q2_touches: Touches: the committee seat assignment process
constitutional_questions.q2_where: the committee assignment run — each member's normalized vote share is displayed beside the tie-break so the math is auditable on sight.
constitutional_questions.q3_answer_a: a legislature sizing law (v1: cube-root only) — total seats =
constitutional_questions.q3_answer_b: over the summed direct-children population, with no ceiling on the total. Future alternative laws reserved.
constitutional_questions.q3_surfaced: the constitution bounds a district (5–9 seats) but is silent on how many population-apportioned seats a parent legislature should have in total.
constitutional_questions.q3_touches: Touches: independent election boards (min 5 / max 9 seats per district + subdivision)
constitutional_questions.q3_where: the district mapper derives every seat budget from the sizing law and displays the quota (population ÷ seats) beside it. At Earth scale the law yields 1,999 population-apportioned seats across 282 districts — a number the constitutional text never had to confront.
constitutional_questions.q4_answer_a: districts are composites of direct child jurisdictions, each within the constitutional 5–9 seat range, built from real jurisdictional lines — never free-form geometry, and never a textbook method. Seats flow from a giant-cascade allocation: the chamber's cube-root total splits to children by population share (with the children's own sum as the denominator); a child whose share would round past the ceiling locks to its nearest whole at once, and its budget redistributes among the rest, layer by layer. Drawn districts then round to the
constitutional_questions.q4_answer_b: whole independently — the chamber size is fixed, so a drawing whose seats miss the pool budget is a defect to be redrawn, never a rounding to be forced. Where a jurisdiction exceeds the ceiling with no child subdivisions in the dataset, district lines must be drawn manually — the open frontier.
constitutional_questions.q4_surfaced: free-form line-drawing fights community integrity and auditability — and no textbook apportionment method (Webster, Sainte-Laguë, largest-remainder) keeps seat counts faithful to a chamber size that the cube-root law fixes exactly.
constitutional_questions.q4_touches: Touches: independent election boards ("drawn equally, contiguously, and fairly") · subdivision of legislatures
constitutional_questions.q4_where: the district mapper renders draft / active / archived plans with nearest-rounded seats, contiguity and integrity indicators, and the optimal / suboptimal / current grouping stats; election-board observation runs through the board console. There is no Webster or Sainte-Laguë step anywhere in the allocation.
constitutional_questions.q5_answer: two-phase elections: continuous approval → finalist cutoff → time-boxed ranked window → one-count PR-STV (Droop quota, Gregory fractional transfers) filling all seats per district.
constitutional_questions.q5_surfaced: a continuous, filterable approval phase (opening the moment the prior election certifies) with a finalist line (top X per race, scaled to the seat count) makes the right-to-stand guarantee operational at planetary candidate counts — while write-in of any validated candidate preserves the right absolutely.
constitutional_questions.q5_touches: Touches: the right to vote and stand for election · the right to stand for office
constitutional_questions.q5_where: the open ballot (the finalist line, revocable approvals, jockeying deltas) and the ranked ballot with its always-available write-in of any validated candidate.
constitutional_questions.q6_answer: countback runs universally — the prior election's ballots are re-run with the vacated member removed as a candidate, with no faction filtering anywhere in the procedure. Failure still falls through to a special election within 90–180 days.
constitutional_questions.q6_surfaced: the countback procedure leaned on the faction layer — and with factions replaced by polymorphic endorsements (entry #1), the faction-scoped parts of the procedure no longer mean anything.
constitutional_questions.q6_touches: Touches: the countback procedure for filling vacancies
constitutional_questions.q6_where: the countback engine view and its flow walkthrough.
constitutional_questions.q7_answer: each kind must meet its own peg quorum and pass independently — a majority of ALL serving members of that kind (supermajority where the act type requires it). Needs resolving in the constitutional text.
constitutional_questions.q7_h: 7 · Bicameral dual agreement — the per-kind threshold
constitutional_questions.q7_surfaced: the rule requires both kinds of members to agree independently but names no per-kind threshold or quorum. The intent is to preserve the equal-parts and population-proportional parts over the existing boundaries of the nation-state system, with dual agreement required.
constitutional_questions.q7_touches: Touches: independent agreement for legislative actions · pegging the quorum requirement to full membership
constitutional_questions.q7_where: the dual-agreement meters on bill detail (bicameral toggle).

constitutional_questions.status_legend_a: — proposed for the post-game redraft of
constitutional_questions.status_legend_b: and the workbooks. Entries adopted by a redraft will be re-badged rather than removed, preserving the question's history.

public_records.hardened_chip: Record-keeping cannot be suspended under emergency powers · nothing is publishable-optional · Art. II §2 · WF-SYS-03

translation_review.can_verify_body: Verification is gated to the people who actually read a language — not a central team, and not machine translation grading itself.
translation_review.intro_a: The machine writes the first round. You correct it. Enough verifications move a string to
translation_review.intro_b: — {quorum} readers, not one, so no single person's reading settles what the constitution says in this language.
translation_review.no_draft: no draft — this string falls back to English
translation_review.nobody_verified: Nobody has verified {name} yet. Every string in this language is still exactly what a machine wrote.
translation_review.nothing_here: There is nothing here to review yet.
translation_review.nothing_waiting: Nothing waiting in {label}. Every string here has enough agreement.
translation_review.pick_a: Pick a content type to review it. Interface and page copy cover the screens; audio and captions cover the guide videos.
translation_review.pick_b: overall is the mean of all six — the empty ones count, which is the point of splitting them.
translation_review.queue_gloss_a: Each string shows the English source and the machine's first draft. Accept a good one, or suggest a better wording. Enough verifications move it to
translation_review.queue_quarantined: Strings the machine itself refused to ship — a placeholder went missing, a legal citation changed, the meaning came back too short — are first.
translation_review.reading_body: Verification is gated to the people who read {name} — someone who cannot read a language cannot usefully confirm it. This takes nothing from you: name {name} among your languages on your record and you can start immediately.
translation_review.reading_strong: You are reading this queue, not ruling on it.
translation_review.terms_gloss_a: These words carry legal weight and must read the same everywhere. Settle them first: every string containing one inherits the choice, and re-wording one later unsettles every verdict that was given against the old wording.
translation_review.terms_gloss_b: — a rendering a machine proposed is a draft here too.
translation_review.unworded: {n} have no {name} wording at all, so every string using them was translated with nothing holding it consistent.
translations.add_langs_profile: Add the languages you read on your profile to start verifying — the queue is gated to readers so a translation is only ever settled by people who can judge it.
translations.add_language_body: Don’t see yours? Any of the {n} mapped languages can be opened for translation, and a new one can be requested. The machine drafts every kind of content at once, then it opens for your review — never shipped as final until readers confirm it.
translations.all_carried: Every registered language carries every message.
translations.by_namespace_note: Messages per area of the app, and how many of them each language carries. A namespace maps to a page folder.
translations.can_verify: You can verify — pick a language to work its queue, worst-first:
translations.code_c0: Catalog file could not be parsed
translations.code_c2: Key present in a locale but not in English
translations.code_c4: ID token or citation not byte-identical
translations.code_c5: Message does not compile in vue-i18n
translations.code_c7: PHP and JS locale lists disagree
translations.findings_run_b: for the per-key detail behind each code.
translations.gate_passes: The gate passes. No language is behind and every message compiles.
translations.halt_note: Workers stop at their next committed chunk — at most one chunk is redone.
translations.intro_a: How much of this application a person can read in their own language. Every figure below is produced by the translation gate
translations.intro_b: — the same run that fails a build when a language falls behind. Nothing on this page is measured a second way.
translations.matrix_caption: Translation coverage by language and kind of content

translations.matrix_gloss_d: with catalogs on this instance are shown — a row of dashes for the rest would bury these.
translations.not_measured_b: and exits non-zero while any language is behind.
translations.not_measured_body: No coverage artifact on this instance. Run the gate to produce one:
translations.operator_note: As operator you can verify every language — use this to unstick a queue no reader has reached yet, never to overrule the readers of a language.
translations.overall_note: Overall is the mean of all six kinds, so the four we do not yet produce pull it down. That is deliberate: a language is not translated because its buttons are.
translations.owed: {n} message-translations are still owed across the languages below.
translations.pkg_export_hint: Pick the language the translation is for. The zip holds the English strings that language still lacks. Or export the English master: every source string, no target.
translations.pkg_import_hint: Upload a translated zip or a single JSON file and name its language. The server checks it first and shows what it would accept before anything is written. English is never imported.
translations.pkg_intro: Every package you export is English. Pick the language a translator will produce and the zip holds the English strings that language still lacks, with surface context and the glossary. Translate anywhere, then import the result under that language. Every action runs as a queued job, never in the page.
translations.pkg_request_hint: Record a language nobody has opened yet. It appears in the list below.
translations.pkg_source_option: English master (en) · the source, every string
translations.pkg_state_line: In the app now: English (the source, {keys} strings in {files} files), {present} machine drafts in progress, {absent} registered languages with no strings yet.
translations.same_english_body: counts values byte-identical to the source — a proper noun that legitimately does not translate, or a string nobody has translated yet. It is a hint for reviewers, not a failure.
translations.sign_up_after: and set the languages you read on your profile to start verifying.
translations.six_kinds_note: Interface and page copy are measured here. The other four are produced outside this app and are reported as not-started rather than left blank — a blank cell reads as "fine", which would be a lie.
translations.sop1_detail: Any of the {n} registered languages, or request a new one.
translations.sop2_detail: The machine drafts everything at once — people never start from a blank box.
translations.sop3_detail: Readers of that language see the drafts and begin verifying.
translations.sop4_detail: A string settles once enough readers agree and the gate is clean.
translations.sop_private: Private records never enter the pipeline — a database check forbids it.
translations.sop_verified: Verified by the people who read the interface in that language, never by the machine grading itself.
translations.verifier_gloss: Anyone who reads a language can verify its translations. A draft is settled by a quorum of readers who agree — the machine never publishes itself. The languages you read come from your account and give weight to your verifications.
translations.verifier_role: Verifier role · readers of a language
translations.worker_note: Each worker holds its own copy of the translation model, so the GPU — not the CPU — sets how many can run at once. Work commits in small batches: halting, or a crash, costs at most one batch and never leaves a half-written language.
